current_episode.title: How to Get Funding for a Business with Dan Cholewinski #186

guest.bio_context: Dan Cholewinski started his career in financial services at age 18, beginning in data administration before moving into underwriting at 19 and telesales at 20. He joined a growing motor finance lender at 21, becoming the first salesperson in a new national accounts division at 23 and taking on his first leadership role managing a field sales team at 26. He spent 15 years at that company, seeing it grow from approximately 65-70 employees to around 600, before co-founding Vast Commercial Finance with a business partner.

context.real_quote: If I feel I'm not making enough sales, it's because I'm not talking to enough strangers — as simple as that. Being sat behind the desk being really good at something isn't gonna bring you a whole load of sales.

pending_qa.q: What is Dan Cholewinski's view on apprenticeships versus university education for career development?
pending_qa.r: Dan is a self-described 'big advocate of the apprentice system,' arguing that it provides practical experience combined with learning simultaneously. He believes university is not necessary for most careers — though he acknowledges it may be required for professions like medicine — and that the current education system is too one-size-fits-all, favouring theoretical over practical application.
